slides.title: Artists make great places
slides.sub: Nightlife as infrastructure for agency, talent and place.
slides.meta: UKDF Fellowship proposal · Carly Heath, Nightlife Culture

slides.title: Places don’t make great artists. Artists make great places.
slides.body: Britain’s cultural dynamism begins when people gather around music, experiment, organise and create something that belongs to their time and place.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Single statement; no diagram.

slides.title: Nightlife is culture
slides.body: The gathering places for collective joy are also talent incubators, knowledge banks and cultural value generators. Nightlife is a precious asset to British creativity and global reputation.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: People-centred scene photography; three short value labels. [Photo slot reserved.]

slides.title: How the night becomes a dynamic place
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Large causal pathway; short examples under each stage.

slides.title: The system sees nightlife too late
slides.body: Formal systems recognise the artist, destination, economic return or crisis. The relationships, gathering places and cultural labour that made them possible are harder to see and support.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Two-layer timeline: where culture begins / where systems arrive.

slides.title: The connective infrastructure is thin
bullets: Local advocates keep rebuilding evidence and political backing from the beginning.
Decision-makers see partial pictures of nightlife’s value.
Funders and responsible investors struggle to find locally legitimate people and propositions.
Research, policy, advocacy and delivery remain too disconnected.
slides.job: Name the problem UKDF can move.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Four linked gaps converging on one missing bridge.

slides.title: Nationally relevant infrastructure that increases hyperlocal power
slides.body: Build a shared way for local cultural knowledge to become credible evidence, stronger advocacy, practical policy routes and investable action — while preserving the agency and distinctiveness of place.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: National network composed of distinct local nodes; avoid generic map pins.

slides.title: Meet Nightlife Culture
slides.body: Nightlife Culture is a creative policy, research and design studio working across nightlife, music, culture, place and the systems that shape them.
slides.body2: A creative policy studio for nightlife, music, culture and cities. Built for people who know that collective joy deserves serious evidence, policy design and investment.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Studio definition plus short proposition and audience-belief line.

slides.title: Enough rigour for institutions. Enough cultural truth for the people who make the night.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Dancefloor-to-decision-room bridge using two photographic worlds. [Photo slot reserved.]

slides.body: Because she can move between the dancefloor, the committee room, the funder meeting and the evidence base without losing the truth of the culture.

bullets: Bristol’s first Night Time Economy Advisor and founder of Bristol Nights

slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Evidence-led timeline; concise proof points.

slides.title: A Ticket to the Future
slides.body: A collaborative response to a systemic problem: how Bristol’s music community can create an enduring source of investment and have a meaningful say in its own future. Developed through design thinking, restorative economics and a process centred on the music community.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Journey from shared problem to CBS and future member governance.

slides.title: From Bristol delivery to transferable infrastructure
lanes: supports establishment of the Community Benefit Society and Bristol delivery.
supports the distinct inquiry, evidence and method that can help more local cultural communities build power.
slides.job: Separate the funding roles and extract learning.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Two connected lanes with a clean boundary.

slides.title: Five inquiry strands
panels: Explore nightlife as an informal talent programme: where people develop agency, identity, craft, confidence, networks, collaboration and leadership before formal systems recognise them.
Trace how artists, organisers, venues, crews, advocates and sonic communities create the distinct cultural life, reputation and future possibility of place.

Follow how cultural, social, civic and economic value is created, where it travels, who captures it and which contributors remain under-resourced. A Ticket to the Future provides a live restorative-economics case.

Develop and test the foundations of the proposed Nightlife Cultural Value Index and other practical tools that help local advocates, policymakers, funders and investors see, strengthen and act on nightlife’s value.
Test how Nightlife Culture can hold the method, maintain cultural legitimacy, convene specialist capacity and turn learning into future commissions, research and sector infrastructure.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Five generous panels; no dense wheel.

slides.title: The Nightlife Cultural Value Index
slides.body: The Nightlife Cultural Value Index is a proposed shared evidence layer for the cultural life of the night. It helps advocates, places, funders and researchers connect people, scenes, spaces, value and conditions for action.
slides.job: Frame the proposal with ambition and discipline.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Layered evidence architecture with distinct local inputs.

slides.title: A 10–12 month fellowship
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Overlapping 12-month timeline; phase outcomes beneath the bars.

slides.title: Evidence that creates new capability
bullets: Local advocates can make stronger cases and shape action.
Places can see the cultural life of the night more clearly.
Funders can find credible people and propositions.
Researchers and sector bodies can connect local learning.
Nightlife Culture can hold and expand the work.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: Five audience outcomes; people first.

slides.title: What UKDF makes possible
slides.body: Protected founder capacity, informed challenge and specialist expertise to synthesise two decades of practice, test the first method in the field, develop the NCVI evidence layer and establish the institution and next-stage proposition.
slides.visual: VISUAL DIRECTION: One joined resource flowing into four step-change outcomes.

bullets: £50k flexible programme resource across six phases
